title: Kickoff notes — Private upgrade + rollback mechanism (VPC + on‑prem)
content:
Doc: working notes from kickoff. Not a spec.

Meeting
- Date/time: 2025-05-06 10:00–11:00 PT
- Facilitator: Talia Benson
- Goal of meeting: align on scope, success criteria, and first-pass constraints for “Private upgrade + rollback mechanism” (installer + charts + Terraform + platform gating)

Attendees (partial)
- Vivek Kulkarni (Product owner, Private Deployments)
- Connor O’Brien (Release Engineering)
- Ethan Park (Platform Control Plane)
- Irene Choi (Infra)
- Sean Gallagher (SRE)
- Fatima Noor (On‑prem/air‑gapped constraints)
- Sahana Iyer (CI/integration tests)
- Allison Grant (Observability/audit signals)
- Dev Patel (Support readiness)
- Markus Klein (Solutions/design partner coordination)

Why we’re doing this (problem statement)
- Private customers treat upgrades as risky events; current process is too “tribal knowledge” and inconsistently executed across VPC vs on‑prem.
- Upgrade incidents/near‑misses have clustered around:
  - DB migrations that lock too long / fail mid-flight (see Jira SUP-18421)
  - incomplete backups or backups that aren’t restorable under pressure
  - drifted Helm values / manual changes leading to non-deterministic upgrade behavior
  - on‑prem customers struggling with air‑gapped artifacts, checksum/manifest mismatches (see SUP-18510)
  - insufficient storage headroom causing snapshot failures or PV expansion issues (see SUP-18577)

High-level goals (from Vivek / PM direction)
- Safe-by-default upgrade workflow for Redwood Private (VPC and on‑prem)
- Consistent, versioned workflow with strong prechecks and clear failure modes
- Deterministic rollback entry points + clear semantics (what is guaranteed, what is best-effort)
- Auditable artifacts for enterprise: upgrade plan, executed steps, backup/restore status, customer-facing changelog
- Default supported path: N-1 → N (multi-hop later)

Non-goals (explicitly called out)
- Full automated upgrade across multiple major versions (for now)
- Magical handling of every historical schema edge case (we will document “manual intervention required” when needed)

Operator UX (agreed direction, not final)
- Primary interface: redwood-private-installer CLI (works both VPC + on‑prem)
- Installer should output an “upgrade plan artifact” that is saved and can be attached to support bundles
- Dry-run mode needed for customers to validate artifacts/prechecks before a maintenance window

Proposed upgrade phases (whiteboard)
1) Plan + preflight
   - Generate staged plan based on from_version → to_version, environment (VPC vs on‑prem), and enabled features
   - Run prechecks (blocking vs warning)
   - Validate artifact availability (online registries or offline bundle)
2) Backup
   - Snapshot / logical backup depending on storage backend + customer constraints
   - Verify backup completion and record identifiers
3) Control plane upgrade
   - Upgrade CP components first, complete readiness gates
   - Apply DB migrations under guardrails (timeouts, idempotency)
4) Data plane upgrade
   - Roll DP workloads in safe order (per charts), with readiness checks + timeouts
5) Post-upgrade verification
   - Health checks + smoke tests
   - Emit audit events and persist “upgrade result” summary

Rollback model (initial, to be locked in ADR)
- Rollback is a distinct command, driven by stored upgrade state + plan:
  - “rollback to last known good” when the plan recorded a backup point
  - should be idempotent (can re-run rollback)
- Important nuance noted by Ethan/Sean:
  - Rollback after schema migrations is the sharp edge; we need a contract for backward-compatible migrations or explicit guardrails (see redwood#29210)
  - If we can’t guarantee full DB down-migration, we must define supported rollback windows/conditions (e.g., rollback allowed only before certain migration stage completes)

Constraints / requirements raised in kickoff
On‑prem / air‑gapped (Fatima)
- Customers may not have:
  - internet access
  - external DNS resolution beyond their internal network
  - access to public registries
- Offline bundle must include:
  - container images or references to offline registry
  - Helm charts
  - manifest + checksums/signatures
  - explicit “what versions are inside” metadata
- Installer must do local verification and be loud about mismatch (checksum/signature) and missing artifacts

SRE and operability (Sean)
- Precheck quality matters more than feature breadth; we should make a small set of checks extremely reliable.
- Explicitly distinguish:
  - MUST-BLOCK checks (unsafe to proceed)
  - WARN checks (proceed with acknowledgement)
- Upgrade should integrate with our observability “upgrade window” annotations so we can separate upgrade noise from real incidents.

Release engineering (Connor)
- Version gating and supported upgrade paths must be centrally defined and testable (avoid “it worked in staging once”).
- Private release gating will require evidence: minimal upgrade test matrix and artifacts.
- Need to clarify mapping between installer version and platform version (do we pin installer versions per release train?).

Support readiness (Dev)
- Support asks for:
  - a 1-page “if upgrade fails, do this” decision tree
  - what logs and artifacts to request
  - a support bundle section that includes plan + last run logs + backup identifiers

Initial checklist (v0) — Prechecks
Note: not yet agreed which are blocking. This is the raw list from kickoff.

Cluster / Kubernetes
- Kubernetes version supported by target release (block)
- Node readiness: all nodes Ready; no NotReady > N minutes (block)
- Control plane components healthy (API server reachable; etcd health if customer-managed) (block)
- Critical pods in redwood namespace healthy (block)
- PodDisruptionBudgets not violated / sufficient capacity to roll (warn/block TBD)
- Cluster autoscaler state (warn)
- Admission controllers / PSP replacements / custom policies that could block upgrades (warn)

Storage
- Storage headroom: PV capacity + snapshot requirements + DB volume headroom (block)
- Snapshot support available on backend (EBS/CSI/etc.) (block if chosen backup mode requires it)
- IOPS/throughput adequate for DB migration window (warn)

Database + migrations
- DB connectivity from installer context and from CP pods (block)
- DB replication/HA status healthy (warn/block TBD)
- Migration lock timeout config within safe default (block if unsafe) (ties to redwood#29210)
- DB free space (block)

Networking + identity
- DNS/TLS: required endpoints resolvable; cert validity not expiring within N days (warn/block TBD)
- OIDC/SSO reachability (warn; debate in meeting about blocking for some environments)
- NTP/clock skew within tolerance (warn)

Artifacts
- Target version artifacts reachable (online mode) (block)
- Offline bundle present + signature verified (air‑gapped mode) (block)
- Helm chart + image tag compatibility (block)

Config drift
- Detect drift in Helm values / manual changes from last applied (warn; might become block later)
- Terraform version pinning present (warn)

Initial checklist (v0) — Backups
- Control plane DB backup (block)
  - logical dump option (Postgres): preferred for portability but takes time
  - snapshot option: faster restore but backend-dependent
- Config/values backup (block)
  - last applied Helm values
  - installer config YAML
  - Terraform state pointers (NOT the state file itself unless customer explicitly opts in)
- Secrets handling (security note)
  - do not export raw secrets by default
  - backup should capture references/identifiers (KMS key ids, secret names) + ensure restore procedure documented
- Artifact cache/model cache
  - clarify if we back up cache or treat as ephemeral (lean toward ephemeral + re-warm)

Prior incident learnings (quick recap)
- SUP-18421 (DB migration failure)
  - issue: migration lock lasted too long, workload impact during maintenance window; unclear rollback steps
  - action: implement migration guardrails (timeouts, idempotency) + decision tree for rollback vs retry
- SUP-18510 (air‑gapped verification errors)
  - issue: customers had mismatched bundle + missing docs on what to verify
  - action: offline bundle manifest + checksums/signature verification with explicit error messages and remediation steps
- SUP-18577 (insufficient storage)
  - issue: backup step failed late; maintenance window wasted
  - action: storage headroom precheck must run early and must be blocking

Open questions (captured during meeting)
- Rollback semantics:
  - What are we guaranteeing if schema migrations have run? “Rollback of binaries” vs “full state rollback”
  - Do we require backward-compatible schema for N-1 ↔ N in GA path? If yes, what’s the enforcement mechanism?
- Backup scope:
  - Do we support both snapshot and logical dump always, or select based on backend?
  - Minimum retention period? (enterprise asks for X days vs operator wants to delete quickly)
- Upgrade plan artifact:
  - where stored (on disk vs cluster secret/configmap vs both)
  - format (JSON schema versioning)
  - what fields are required for compliance audit logs
- Prechecks policy:
  - final list of blocking checks
  - whether OIDC reachability blocks or warns (context: some customers allow local break-glass during maintenance)
- Downtime expectations:
  - are we targeting “no downtime” for VPC? (seems unrealistic for initial in-place upgrade)
  - what’s our official comms language for maintenance windows?
- Testing:
  - minimum e2e matrix for gating (k8s versions, storage backends, VPC vs on‑prem, air‑gapped)
  - how to reduce flake in upgrade tests (timeouts vs deterministic fixtures)

Decisions made in kickoff (soft decisions; confirm in ADR)
- Start with N-1 → N as the supported upgrade path for GA.
- Split control plane vs data plane rollout phases (ordering enforced by charts + installer plan).
- Prechecks + backup are mandatory phases (no “skip” without explicit override flags and audit logging).

Action items (week 1)
- Vivek: confirm success metrics + GA requirements list (tie to PM-812)
- Connor: draft release gating checklist for Private upgrades; propose minimum CI evidence
- Sean + Allison: propose initial upgrade observability signals + audit events required
- Fatima: provide top 5 on‑prem constraints from design partners (air‑gapped specifics)
- Sahana: propose initial CI test matrix + where to run nightly vs PR-gated
- Talia: create running doc for open questions + owners; schedule ADR review meeting

Notes to self (Talia)
- Keep this doc lightweight; move “hard decisions” into ADR ASAP.
- We need a crisp customer-facing definition of rollback. Avoid overpromising.
- Biggest risk: schema migration rollback story. Make sure ownership is explicit (Ethan + Michael Nguyen?).

Appendix: quick glossary
- CP = control plane components (API, controllers, DB migrations)
- DP = data plane / serving plane (inference workloads, gateways)
- Plan artifact = versioned JSON output from installer describing stages/steps + rollback hooks
